name: panel-economics
operates_on: adjudication/ — the engine itself, not a lane's content

hard_constraints: resolved_correct_rate must not fall below the recorded baseline
not_resolved_rate must not rise above the recorded baseline
interactive-work headroom must not fall below 40% of the daily allowance
per_iteration_inputs: adjudication/cost_ledger.py -> actual spend from vendor token counts
metric.note: accuracy.py returns RESOLVED CORRECT / RESOLVED WRONG / NOT RESOLVED. All three are used; folding NOT RESOLVED into either other outcome misreports the instrument.
metric.objective_note: v2.1: seats 1 and 5 are subscription-funded at zero marginal dollar cost, so dollars no longer bound the search. Rate limits do -- routines draw down the same subscription pool as interactive work. See agents/17-subscription-economics.md section 4.

cheat_paths.path: Resolve fewer questions - a panel that answers nothing has an excellent cost per answer
cheat_paths.defence: not_resolved_rate is a hard constraint, not a term. A run that raises it is rejected before its cost is scored.
30-question held-out accuracy set the loop never sees. Divergence voids every iteration since the last held-out run.

cheat_paths.path: Weaken a gate so more claims survive and more questions resolve
cheat_paths.defence: gates are immutable. Reordering permitted, weakening is an automatic rollback and escalation.

cheat_paths.path: Lower max_tokens until answers truncate - cost falls, quality falls invisibly
cheat_paths.defence: truncation is detected and counted as RESOLVED WRONG, never as a saving. test_truncation.py exists.

cheat_paths.path: Shift work onto the subscription seats until rate limits throttle Andrew's own interactive sessions - the dollar metric improves while the real resource is exhausted
cheat_paths.defence: interactive headroom is a hard constraint, not a term. Usage draw is the primary objective precisely so this path cannot be taken.

held_out.description: Full accuracy.py on the 30-question set, once per 20 iterations and at the end, gated by ACCURACY_CONFIRM=yes. Costs $148.80-$504.60. Held-out wins any disagreement with the per-iteration proxy, and voids every iteration since the last held-out run.

blockers.what: rates.json flags seat_3's Mistral model id as UNVERIFIED and notes Magistral is retired. A ceiling computed from an unchecked price bounds nothing.
blockers.clear_by: Confirm the id in the Mistral console or by a diagnostic call that echoes the served model, then set _model, max_input_tokens and verified_on in rates.json.

blockers.what: rates.json says re-check every 90 days. Verified 2026-09-09, so due 2026-12-08.
blockers.clear_by: Re-read each vendor pricing page, update verified_on.

stop_early_if: 15 consecutive iterations with no improvement, or any held-out disagreement
production_limits_note: Effective only once pilot.passed is true.

pilot.note: Playbook p.18. Production caps unlock only after a supervised pilot passes. A sentence in a prompt is not a hard budget - the runner needs a tested timeout, attempt counter and spend guard.
